va_middle_sunset_wall.blurb: Middle Sunset Wall is the biggest section of the Sunset Walls, a granite cliff on Old Rag in Shenandoah National Park. It holds 18 routes, a little over half trad and the rest sport, with a few usable on top rope. Almost everything is stiff: a handful of climbs sit at 5.8 and 5.9, the bulk fall around 5.11 with several 5.12s, and there is a single 5.14 at the top end. The cliff as a whole faces northwest and stays shaded much of the day, so it works as a summer option on the mountain. It is a long hike in, so plan for a full outing.

wa_wayne_s_world.blurb: Wayne's World is a steep dry-tooling and mixed crag off the I-90 corridor near North Bend, under an hour from Seattle. Nearly all of the 18 climbs here are mixed lines, mostly M6 to M8 with one at M4, and a few bolted lines graded in rock-climbing numbers run from 5.10 into the 5.12 range. Routes are short and bolted, and rain or snow does not shut the crag down, which makes it a year-round training spot. The stone is chossy, so expect loose holds and keep an eye on who is below you. Hold-breaking is frowned on; use monopoint crampons or rock shoes.

wa_kenticle_proper_the.blurb: The Kenticle Proper is a freestanding artificial climbing wall beside the East Hill skate park in Kent, around 50 feet tall, with textured, featured surfaces and removable holds. It is a quick stop for a workout rather than a destination crag. Most of the 18 lines are sport, with a few top-rope lines and one boulder problem; grades run from 5.6 to about 5.10, with 5.10 the most common and a good number of easier climbs mixed in. The wall mostly faces east and west and gets sun nearly all day, with one tree shading a few lines and the north side often damp. Lines are reset fairly often, so the lineup changes.

wa_airfield_the.blurb: The Airfield is a bouldering area in the Icicle Creek zone near Leavenworth, reached by a hike up past Playground Point. It has about 18 problems here, spread widely across the grades: a good run of V1 to V5, a few V6 and V7, and one standout V10. The area is sunny, scenic and usually quiet, with solid rock and mostly good landings, which makes it a pleasant alternative to the busier Icicle circuits. The final stretch of trail can get overgrown, so long pants help. Allow extra time on the first visit since the way in is easy to lose.

wa_rainbow_rocks.blurb: Rainbow Rocks is an andesite crag on a hillside above the Tieton River, along Highway 12 in south-central Washington. Most of its 18 routes are bolted, with a few cracks; grades start around 5.7 and run to the low 5.12s, with the bulk at 5.9 and 5.10. The columns run from steep slabs to mildly overhanging faces, roughly 35 to 60 feet tall, and the many horizontal edges suit footwork-focused climbing. The face sits in shade early and bakes once summer sun arrives, and its ridge-top position makes windy days unpleasant. It sees fewer visitors than the other main Tieton crags.

wa_moon_rocks.blurb: Moon Rocks is a compact cliff of andesite columns, found in the lower canyon on the Tieton River's south bank. Climbing here is mainly trad, with long, steep crack lines and a handful of bolted routes among the 18 listed. Grades run from about 5.6 to 5.12, but most are 5.10 and 5.11, so it suits climbers already comfortable with cracks. Many lines can be top-roped from a ledge above, reached by a gully on the left side. The cliff is shaded for most of the day and catches sun in late afternoon. The canyon is dry, with sagebrush, and rattlesnakes are a concern.

wa_amazonia.blurb: Amazonia is a clean, slightly overhanging sport wall on the Mt Washington trail near North Bend, off I-90 Exit 38. Of its 18 routes, 17 are bolted and one is trad, and the grades cluster tightly: nearly all are 5.10, with a couple of 5.9s, one 5.8 and a single 5.11. The rock is solid and jug-heavy, and there is a roomy belay platform. It ranks among the most popular 5.10 walls at Exit 38, so weekends bring crowds. Seepage is common and the wall takes much of the summer to dry, so it climbs best in the warm months, when the shade is welcome.
